Opening position from the studio on the three draft clauses. We can work with the structure as written; the gaps are in scope, clocks, and what "retained for quality control" actually authorizes.

**1. Subcontractors — disclose now, name in an annex**

We will use one external color specialist on the first batch only. We would rather name them in the schedule than rely on a general permission. Proposed terms:

- Named subcontractor and named individuals listed in an annex; no substitution without your written approval.
- Flow-down of the full confidentiality schedule, signed, with no further subcontracting and no consumer cloud, personal devices, or third-party AI/enhancement tools.
- Access scoped to the first batch, expires at batch acceptance, transfer over encrypted channel with logs we can produce on request.
- Your right to strike the name and require the work be done in-house or on your premises (see below).

Tell us whether the donor deeds impose restrictions that flow to third parties regardless of our contract — if donors barred any off-site handling, that changes the design, not just the paperwork.

**2. What the color specialist actually needs, and the fallback**

Our preference is full-frame, uncropped master images at native resolution with the color target in frame. Crops remove the target and the illumination gradient across the platen, which is exactly what calibration corrects; working from crops means guessing at the edges and re-scanning later.

If full masters leaving the building is unacceptable, in order of our preference:

- **(a) Target-plus-strip package.** You or we generate, on your site, a color target capture per lighting setup plus narrow uncalibrated strips across each sheet (edge-to-edge, low resolution). Specialist returns correction profiles only; no letter content leaves. Costs us a half-day of on-site capture per batch and gives slightly weaker edge correction.
- **(b) Specialist on your premises**, your hardware, your network, supervised, no removable media. Cleanest for you, adds roughly two days and travel to the first batch.
- **(c) We calibrate in-house** against a reference you supply. No third party at all, but we cannot guarantee tone match to your reading-room expectations, and we would want that limitation written into the acceptance criteria.

We will accept (a) or (b) without a price fight. We would resist a term that permits subcontracting in name but leaves the specialist nothing usable to work on.

**3. Access and deletion schedule — concrete numbers**

- **Day 0:** batch delivered to you, masters transferred to your custody. We keep working derivatives and correction files only.
- **Day 0–10 business days:** our correction window. Studio access limited to the named operators on the batch; specialist access ends at Day 0.
- **Acceptance:** written acceptance, or acceptance deemed at the end of Day 10 if you have raised no defects. If you raise defects, the window restarts for the affected items only.
- **Acceptance + 5 business days:** all working files, derivatives, caches, and specialist-side copies deleted. Certificate of deletion listing volumes and file counts, signed by us and countersigned by the specialist.
- **Backups:** our rotation is 45 days, so residual copies age out no later than deletion + 45 days. During that period: no restore of pilot material except full-system disaster recovery, and if a restore occurs, pilot paths are re-deleted before the system returns to service, with notice to you. Second certificate at expiry.

If 45 days of residual tail is too long for unpublished donor material, we can segregate the pilot onto a dedicated backup set with a 14-day rotation. That is a real cost and slightly higher restore risk for us, so we would want it priced as a line item rather than absorbed — but it is available, and it cuts the outer bound from roughly 60 days after delivery to about 29.

We do not propose keeping masters after acceptance. If you want a second copy held anywhere, that should be your escrow, not our QC clause.

**4. Publicity**

We accept written consent as a precondition and will not publish without it. Our ask is narrow: one process image, anonymized, no legible text, no donor names, no identifying handwriting, no geolocation or capture metadata, caption language pre-agreed, single use on our project page, no licensing onward.

Our first proposal is equipment-only — scanner, cradle, color target, gloved hands, no collection material in frame. That should need no donor analysis at all. If you want material visible for it to read as a real process image, we can offer an extreme crop of a blank margin or a non-text area at a resolution where nothing is reconstructable, submitted to you for approval before publication.

Please give us a decision clock — 10 business days to approve or refuse a submitted image, silence treated as refusal, not consent. And confirm whether donor consent is yours to obtain or something we must be shown evidence of. If the answer is that no image of this collection can be published in any form, say so now and we will shoot a generic setup rather than negotiate a refusal later.

Priority order for us: the correction window and the deletion certificates are non-negotiable operational needs; the color pathway is flexible; the image is the item we will trade away first.

We can accept the 10-business-day correction window and use your target-plus-strip approach with one change. The restriction on two collections follows the viewer, including on our premises. We propose the following terms for the signed schedule.

1. **Calibration and specialist access.** The archive will identify the two restricted collections to the named studio operators before capture. For those collections, use the archive’s calibration sheet to capture the target and full-platen illumination gradient under each lighting setup. Only those calibration captures may go to the specialist. For other first-batch collections, the specialist may also receive masked images or strips after the archive checks the exact export and approves it in writing. Masking must permanently remove handwriting and identifying content, including from metadata and embedded previews. The specialist returns correction profiles only. We accept your annex, signed confidentiality terms, tool restrictions, encrypted transfer and access logs. The archive retains its right to withdraw approval. Specialist access ends at first-batch delivery or earlier withdrawal.

2. **Quality control and deletion.** Day 0 is confirmed delivery of the masters to the archive. The studio deletes its active master copies that day. Named operators may retain only the derivatives and correction files needed to resolve defects. We accept deemed acceptance after 10 business days without a defect notice. A timely notice keeps only the affected items open, with a fresh review window on corrected delivery. Delete studio working copies, including caches, within five business days of acceptance. The specialist deletes its copies when its access ends. The studio’s deletion certificate must identify the batch, volumes, file counts and deletion dates and include the specialist’s countersignature.

3. **Backups and incidents.** Use the dedicated 14-calendar-day rotation, with final backup expiry within 14 calendar days of active deletion and a second certificate confirming expiry. We accept the proposed disaster-recovery controls and restore notice. Please quote the dedicated set separately. **The line-item price remains open.** Before signature, each party will list a named incident lead, monitored email and urgent phone number. The studio must notify the archive lead promptly, within 24 hours of discovering suspected unauthorized access, disclosure, loss or missed deletion, including at the specialist. Send the affected batch and containment steps then, with updates as facts become available.

4. **Publicity.** An equipment-only photograph is eligible for approval. Use a generic setup with all collection material out of frame, including in screens and reflections. Submit the metadata-stripped image, exact caption and intended project page. We will respond within 10 business days. Only express written archive approval permits that single use, with no onward licensing. Silence is refusal. The archive handles any donor clearance it considers necessary. A margin or other collection crop falls outside this permission.

Please confirm that the calibration-sheet capture gives the specialist enough information to assess edge correction for the two restricted collections. If it leaves a measurable tone-match limitation, identify the affected acceptance criterion before signature so we can resolve that specific exception.

Confirming the calibration question first, since it drives one acceptance criterion.

**1. Does the calibration-sheet capture give the specialist enough?**

For edge correction, yes — provided the capture protocol is fixed in the annex rather than left to the operator:

- Archive's calibration sheet must be full-platen sized, matte, spectrally neutral, and free of optical brighteners. If the sheet is a common office stock with OBAs, the white point will drift under different lamps and the specialist will calibrate to the sheet, not to your illuminant.
- One capture per lighting setup per session, same platen height, focus, aperture, and lamp warm-up state as the production scans; sheet placed in the same plane as the document surface. Any change of lamp, diffusion, or glass triggers a new capture.
- Target in frame at a fixed position, plus one bare-sheet frame with no target for the gradient map.

With that, the specialist can build a per-setup flat-field and profile that corrects falloff and cast across the full platen, and we can verify it numerically on the sheet.

**The residual limitation, stated precisely:** the sheet is not the substrate. We cannot assess paper base tone, translucency, show-through, or ink density on the two restricted collections without seeing the material, and neither can the specialist. So the limitation is *substrate-referenced tone match*, not edge correction.

**Affected criterion — proposed exception, to be settled before signature:**

- Split the color acceptance criterion into (i) *capture-system accuracy* and (ii) *substrate tone match*.
- For (i), all collections including the restricted two: mean ΔE00 ≤ 2 and max ≤ 4 on the target patches, measured on the archive's calibration sheet and target under each setup. This we warrant.
- For (ii), the restricted two only: white point and tone curve are set by the archive on the archive-held masters at review. We do not warrant a numerical substrate match we cannot measure; we warrant to implement your written tone direction and re-deliver. Your visual judgment governs, and a tone objection is a valid defect notice, not a dispute.
- For all other first-batch collections, (ii) stays as originally drafted since the specialist sees approved masked strips.

If you want a hard number on (ii) for the restricted two, the only honest route is an archive operator measuring a substrate patch on your side and sending us the values — numbers only, no image. We can work to that.

**2. Day 0 master deletion versus the correction window**

Deleting active masters on confirmed delivery is fine, but it means every correction depends on you handing material back. Two things needed:

- Deletion triggered on your checksum-verified receipt confirmation, same day. If verification is not confirmed, Day 0 has not occurred and the clock has not started.
- A re-export service level: on a defect notice, archive supplies the affected masters or supervised access within **2 business days**. Our correction clock pauses while we wait. Without this, the 10-day window is not ours to control.
- Fresh review window on corrected delivery: **5 business days**, affected items only. Two cycles, then a joint review call rather than an open loop.

**3. Specialist access ending at delivery — one narrow reopening**

As drafted, the specialist is gone at Day 0 but a tone defect may surface on Day 8. We need either profiles validated before delivery, or a way to re-run them. Proposal:

- Profiles delivered and validated against the sheet **before** Day 0. That handles most cases.
- One narrow reopening right during the correction window: written request per lighting setup, archive approval, specialist receives **only the already-approved calibration captures** — no new exports, no collection material, restricted or otherwise. Maximum one re-run per setup. Access ends at acceptance + 5.
- If you refuse reopening entirely, we accept it, but then the (ii) exception above must be explicit: tone corrections on the restricted two are done in-house against your written direction, with no specialist verification.

**4. Masking approval throughput**

Per-export written approval is workable but will eat the window if each export waits in a queue. Ask: **3 business days** to approve or reject an export package, and **standing approval for a mask template** once you have approved its first instance — subsequent exports using the identical template and geometry get logged and notified rather than re-approved item by item. We will supply flattened outputs, no layers, no embedded previews, no thumbnails, metadata stripped and the strip verified by a second operator before submission.

**5. Withdrawal of approval**

Accepted. Consequences to write down: withdrawal stops the affected work, is not a breach by either party, extends the schedule by the stoppage plus re-setup, and we fall back to in-house calibration under the (ii) exception. Costs of work already performed and of re-setup are payable. We would rather agree that now than argue about it mid-batch.

**6. Deletion certificates and the specialist's own backups**

Two loose ends:

- The specialist deletes at Day 0 but countersigns our certificate at acceptance + 5, and again at backup expiry. Its confidentiality undertaking must expressly survive termination of access and carry the countersignature and audit obligations. Please confirm you want that in the flow-down text you review.
- We will attest our dedicated 14-day rotation. The specialist must give a matching attestation: either no backup of pilot material, or a rotation no longer than 14 calendar days with the same restore controls. If their standard rotation is 30 days, the outer bound you negotiated is broken by a party you have not contracted with. We will procure the attestation; tell us if you want it addressed to you directly.

Certificates: batch ID, volume identifiers, file counts, deletion dates, method, signatory. Second certificate confirming final backup expiry within 14 calendar days of active deletion.

**7. Incidents**

24 hours from discovery of suspected unauthorized access, disclosure, loss, or missed deletion, including at the specialist — accepted, and we will flow it down with a shorter internal clock so the specialist reports to us in time. Batch and containment steps in the first notice, updates as facts develop, no waiting for a complete picture.

Ask for reciprocity: if an incident on your side touches pilot masters or our credentials, notify our lead on the same clock. Our exposure and our insurance notice obligations depend on it. Named lead, monitored mailbox, and urgent number from us before signature; we will also name a deputy for out-of-hours.

**8. Quote — dedicated backup set**

Indicative, exclusive of tax, valid 30 days:

- Dedicated set provisioning and segregation: **480** one-off.
- 14-day rotation storage and monitoring, per batch: **220**.
- Two deletion certificates and specialist attestation procurement: **included**.
- On-site specialist option, if you ever invoke it: **620/day** plus travel at cost, two-day minimum.
- Re-export handling on your side is not priced by us; if your 2-business-day service level needs staffing, that is your line.

If you take the standard 45-day rotation instead, the 480 and 220 come off and the outer bound returns to roughly 60 days after delivery. Your call, and we will sign either.

**9. Publicity**

Agreed as you have written it. Equipment-only, generic setup, nothing from the collection in frame including screens, glass reflections, and any print on the wall. We withdraw the margin-crop proposal. We will submit the stripped image, exact caption, and the project page URL together, and treat 10 business days of silence as refusal. Donor clearance is yours.

**Open items before signature, from our side:** the (ii) tone-match exception and whether you want a substrate number; the re-export service level and pause; the reopening right or its explicit refusal; mask-template standing approval and the 3-business-day clock; specialist backup attestation; incident reciprocity; and your decision on the backup line item. Send the two restricted collection identifiers before we schedule capture, and confirm whether the calibration sheet is OBA-free.

We accept the **substrate tone-match exception for the two restricted collections only**. We also select the dedicated 14-calendar-day backup set. Please incorporate the following terms in the signature draft.

1. **Calibration and acceptance.** Include your capture protocol in the annex, including the target and bare-sheet frames for each setup and session. Validate profiles before Day 0. For every collection, the studio warrants mean ΔE00 ≤ 2 and maximum ΔE00 ≤ 4 across the target patches for each setup. For the two restricted collections, the archive will judge substrate tone on its masters and provide written correction directions. A visual tone objection is a valid defect notice, and the studio will correct and redeliver in-house. We require no numerical substrate measurement. The existing substrate criterion applies to the other collections. We will provide the two identifiers privately to the named studio operators before scheduling capture. The sheet’s OBA-free status is unverified. We will verify it or supply a conforming sheet before capture.

2. **Delivery and corrections.** Day 0 is the archive’s confirmation of checksum-verified receipt. The studio deletes active masters that day. We accept the initial 10-business-day review window and will provide the affected masters or supervised access within two business days of a defect notice. The studio’s correction clock pauses while it awaits that access. Each corrected delivery starts a five-business-day review for the affected items only. The studio deletes any re-exported master on checksum-confirmed redelivery. After two correction cycles, unresolved items go to joint review and remain open pending written disposition.

3. **Specialist access and masking.** Specialist access ends at Day 0 or earlier withdrawal. Pre-delivery profile validation and in-house corrections give us a workable route without reopening access. For the restricted collections, only calibration-sheet captures may reach the specialist. For the other collections, we will approve or reject a complete package within three business days. You may batch multiple flattened, stripped, second-operator-checked exports in one submission. Our written approval covers the exact files reviewed. Identical geometry can expose different handwriting on the next letter, so a template approval cannot authorize its release.

4. **Withdrawal.** Stop affected work and specialist access immediately on notice. The archive’s exercise of that right is permitted under the schedule. For a discretionary withdrawal, we will pay for conforming work performed and reasonable re-setup costs agreed in writing before they are incurred. Extend the affected dates by the actual stoppage and agreed re-setup time. If studio or specialist noncompliance caused the withdrawal, the studio bears the resulting re-setup cost. Any fallback affecting another collection’s acceptance criterion requires separate written agreement.

5. **Deletion and price.** Studio QC files remain due for deletion within five business days of acceptance. Specialist active copies are due for deletion when access ends. Each party’s backup expiry runs from its own active deletion date. Please obtain a specialist attestation addressed to the archive confirming either zero pilot backups or expiry within 14 calendar days under the agreed restore, re-deletion and notice controls. Include surviving confidentiality, audit and countersignature obligations in the flow-down for our review. We accept the proposed certificate fields and require evidence of both active deletion and final backup expiry from the studio and specialist. Please make the **480 one-off and 220 per batch** quote firm and identify the currency and applicable tax before signature. The on-site option is outside this order.

6. **Incidents and publicity.** We accept reciprocal notice promptly and within 24 hours of discovery for an archive-side incident affecting pilot masters or studio credentials. Include both parties’ leads, deputies, monitored mailboxes and urgent numbers before signature. The studio’s clock includes discovery by the specialist. For publicity, submit the equipment-only image, exact caption and project page URL together. A single use requires express written archive approval. Silence after 10 business days is refusal.

The tone-match exception is settled on these terms. Before signature, we still need the firm price details, completed personnel and incident-contact annex, and specialist undertaking and backup attestation.

Signature draft from our side follows your numbering. Four items still need a decision from you; everything else we can close now.

**1. Price — firm**

Currency **EUR**, exclusive of VAT; VAT charged at the applicable rate on our invoice, reverse-charge where available. Firm for this pilot, no indexation, valid for signature within 30 days of this message.

- Dedicated backup set, provisioning and segregation: **480 one-off**, payable on provisioning, non-refundable once provisioned.
- Dedicated 14-day rotation, storage and monitoring: **220 per batch**.
- Batch = one delivery of up to 250 sheets under a single batch ID. Larger deliveries split into additional batch IDs at 220 each; tell us the expected pilot volume so the total is on the face of the order.
- Included at no extra charge: capture protocol and profile validation, masking packages and second-operator checks, both deletion certificates, procurement of the specialist attestation, incident handling.
- Not included: your re-export staffing; discretionary-withdrawal re-setup under clause 4, quoted in writing before incurred.
- On-site specialist option removed from the order as you directed.
- Payment 30 days from invoice.

**2. No reopening — one consequence to settle before signature**

We accept no specialist access after Day 0. That leaves one gap on the *other* collections: if a setup's profile turns out to be wrong after delivery — lamp drift, a glass change we did not catch — we cannot re-run it externally, and clause 4 says a fallback touching another collection's acceptance criterion needs separate written agreement. We would rather pre-agree the fallback now than negotiate it with an open defect.

Proposal, criterion unchanged:

- Any post-Day 0 color correction on any collection is performed in-house by the named operators.
- Re-validation is numeric and unchanged: mean ΔE00 ≤ 2, max ≤ 4 on the target patches for the affected setup, measured on your calibration sheet, evidence supplied with the corrected delivery. The other collections' substrate criterion is untouched.
- Pre-Day 0 gate: a setup whose profile fails validation is not used for capture. No unvalidated setup enters production.

If you accept that, no separate agreement is ever triggered and clause 4's last sentence stays as a true emergency brake. If you do not, tell us what the fallback is, because "in-house only, no external verification" cannot be left undefined for collections that carry a numerical warranty.

**3. Masking — accepted, with a schedule consequence**

Your reasoning on identical geometry is correct and we withdraw the template request. Per-package written approval, exact files only, batching permitted, 3 business days to approve or reject.

Because that approval sits before Day 0, it affects capture scheduling rather than the correction window. Two terms:

- Capture and delivery dates extend day-for-day for any approval taking longer than 3 business days, and for any rejection requiring re-mask and resubmission. Not a breach by either party.
- We will submit in batches of up to 40 exports, flattened, stripped, previews and thumbnails removed, second-operator checked, with a manifest of file names and hashes so your approval can reference the exact set unambiguously.

**4. Sheet and identifiers — scheduling hold**

We cannot schedule capture for the two restricted collections until (a) the identifiers reach the named operators and (b) the sheet is confirmed OBA-free or a conforming sheet is supplied. If verification is not complete, we will capture the unrestricted collections first and hold the restricted two; that reorders the batch but does not change the price. Please confirm you are content with a split batch, or send verification before the capture date so it stays whole.

**5. Deletion evidence — define "evidence" now**

To avoid a certificate you consider insufficient:

- Active deletion: secure erase of the named volumes/paths, with a tool-generated log showing paths, file counts, timestamps and method, plus the signatory declaration. We will supply the log extract, not just the certificate.
- Backup expiry: rotation log extract showing the final generation containing pilot material aging out, with the expiry date, plus the second certificate.
- Specialist: same two evidence sets, attestation addressed to the archive, delivered by us but signed by them, confirming zero pilot backups or expiry within 14 calendar days of their own active deletion under the agreed restore, re-deletion and notice controls.
- Flow-down text will carry surviving confidentiality, audit, countersignature, evidence and incident obligations, and an internal incident report to us within **12 hours** of their discovery so our 24-hour clock to you is achievable. Their undertaking goes to you for review before signature.

**6. Audit scope — one limit we need**

We will accept an audit right in the flow-down and on ourselves. It must be limited to pilot material and pilot systems, on reasonable written notice during business hours, and must not expose other clients' data or our unrelated systems. If you need unannounced access, we would want it triggered by a suspected incident rather than routine. Confirm which you want; we can draft either but not an unlimited right.

**7. Corrections, withdrawal, incidents, publicity**

Accepted as you have drafted them, with two clarifications we will write in:

- Re-exported masters are deleted on checksum-confirmed redelivery; derivatives and correction files for the affected items survive until acceptance + 5 business days, then go with the rest.
- Joint review after two cycles: we will convene within 5 business days of the second unresolved notice. Items remain open pending written disposition, and the deletion clock for those items runs from that disposition, not from the original acceptance.
- Reciprocal 24-hour incident notice, leads and deputies, monitored mailboxes and urgent numbers in the annex.
- Publicity exactly as drafted; margin crop withdrawn. We will submit image, caption and URL within 10 business days of signature, and treat silence as refusal.

**What we will deliver before signature:** completed personnel and incident-contact annex including deputy; specialist undertaking for your review; specialist backup attestation; capture protocol annex; firm price schedule in EUR with VAT treatment and batch count.

**What we need from you:** the two restricted identifiers to the named operators; sheet verification or a conforming sheet; your incident lead, deputy, mailbox and number; decision on clause 2 fallback and clause 6 audit scope; expected pilot volume and whether a split batch is acceptable.

Once the fallback and audit scope are settled we see nothing else open on our side.

We accept the **in-house correction fallback** for all collections. Before capture, each setup must pass validation. After Day 0, only named studio operators may make corrections. Supply the affected setup’s validation results with the corrected delivery, showing mean ΔE00 ≤ 2 and maximum ΔE00 ≤ 4 on the target patches. The sole acceptance exception is substrate tone match for the two restricted collections. The archive judges tone visually and may require correction by written defect notice.

**Audit.** Routine audits of the studio or specialist require reasonable written notice and take place during business hours. A reasonably suspected pilot incident, including a missed deletion, permits an immediate audit without advance notice. Both routes are limited to relevant pilot records and systems and must protect other clients’ information. We accept the proposed deletion and rotation log extracts, signed certificates and specialist attestation. Where the specialist keeps zero backups, its signed confirmation satisfies the backup evidence requirement. Its 12-hour internal reporting deadline runs within the studio’s 24-hour notice period measured from specialist discovery.

**Masking and timing.** We accept packages of up to 40 exports, identified by filename and hash. The three-business-day review starts on receipt of a complete package. Extend affected dates by the actual delay if our review runs late or we request a change beyond the agreed masking requirements. If a submission exposes handwriting or otherwise fails those requirements, the studio must correct and resubmit it. Our review clock restarts on receipt, but the studio receives no automatic extension for that rework. Only the exact files approved in writing may go to the specialist.

**Capture order and price.** We accept capturing eligible collections first while the restricted two await identification and sheet verification, provided each setup passes validation. We will send the identifiers privately to the named operators before capture is scheduled and confirm the sheet is OBA-free or supply a conforming sheet. The split may change capture or delivery dates without increasing the billable batch count.

We accept EUR 480 once on provisioning and EUR 220 per agreed batch of up to 250 sheets, with the quoted VAT treatment and 30-day payment terms. Pilot volume is still unconfirmed. Before signature, we will confirm the sheet count so the order states the billable batch count and total. Provisioning may begin on signature.

We accept the proposed correction and joint-review deadlines. For publicity, the archive’s 10-business-day decision period starts on receipt of the stripped equipment-only image, caption and URL together. Publication requires express written approval for that use.

Before signature, we will provide our incident lead, deputy, monitored mailbox and urgent number for the annex. Please include the masking delay allocation and split-batch pricing above in the execution copy, along with the completed annexes, specialist undertaking and backup attestation.

All accepted. Three drafting points to make the execution copy operable, then we will issue it.

**1. Signature need not wait on volume.** Provisioning on signature and an unconfirmed sheet count pull in opposite directions. Proposal: the order states the firm unit rates (EUR 480 once, EUR 220 per batch of up to 250 sheets, exclusive of VAT, 30 days), and the billable batch count and total are fixed by a one-page written schedule amendment once you confirm the sheet count — before capture is scheduled, not before signature. Provisioning begins on signature; the 480 is invoiced then. If you would rather hold signature until the count is known, that also works, but provisioning and the 14-day set start only when you sign, and capture dates move accordingly.

**2. Split batch, no extra count.** Written as you have it: capturing eligible collections first while the restricted two await identifiers and sheet verification may move capture and delivery dates but does not increase the billable batch count. Batch count is driven by sheet volume alone. Each setup passes validation before its own capture regardless of order.

**3. Masking delay allocation.** Written as you have it: extension for your late review or for a change request beyond the agreed masking requirements; no automatic extension where our submission exposes handwriting or otherwise fails those requirements, and your 3-business-day clock restarts on receipt of the corrected package. We accept that risk. One mechanical point — the second-operator check is our control, so a failure is ours; but if a package fails because the agreed requirements were ambiguous, we will raise the ambiguity in writing before resubmission and treat the resolution as a change request rather than absorb it silently. Say if you want that removed and we will take the allocation unqualified.

Everything else is settled on your terms: in-house-only corrections after Day 0 with per-setup validation evidence at mean ΔE00 ≤ 2 and max ≤ 4; substrate tone match for the restricted two as the sole exception, judged visually and correctable by written defect notice; routine audit on reasonable notice in business hours and immediate audit on reasonably suspected pilot incident including missed deletion, both limited to relevant pilot records and systems with other clients' information protected; zero-backup signed confirmation satisfying the specialist's backup evidence; the 12-hour internal report running inside our 24-hour notice measured from specialist discovery; deletion and rotation log extracts with signed certificates; joint review within 5 business days of the second unresolved notice and the deletion clock for open items running from written disposition; publicity decision period starting on receipt of image, caption and URL together, express approval only, silence refusal.

**We will issue the execution copy containing:**
- Price schedule and the batch-count amendment mechanism above.
- Capture protocol annex: full-platen neutral OBA-free sheet, per-setup per-session target frame and bare-sheet frame, fixed platen height, focus, aperture and lamp warm-up state, new capture on any lamp, diffusion or glass change, pre-Day 0 validation gate.
- Masking annex: packages up to 40 exports, filename-and-hash manifest, flattened and stripped outputs, second-operator check, exact-file approval, delay allocation.
- Access, correction and deletion schedule with Day 0 defined as your checksum-verified receipt confirmation, master deletion that day, 10-business-day review, 2-business-day re-export service level with our clock paused, 5-business-day corrected-delivery review, re-exported master deletion on checksum-confirmed redelivery, active deletion at acceptance + 5 business days, dedicated 14-calendar-day rotation with final expiry within 14 days of our active deletion, both evidence sets, disaster-recovery-only restore with re-deletion before return to service and notice to you.
- Personnel and incident-contact annex: our lead, deputy, monitored mailbox and urgent number, plus the named operators and named specialist individuals; your four fields left for completion.
- Specialist undertaking for your review: flow-down of the full schedule, no further subcontracting, no consumer cloud, personal devices or third-party enhancement tools, encrypted transfer and access logs, access scoped to the first batch ending at Day 0 or earlier withdrawal, correction profiles returned only, active deletion at access end, backup attestation addressed to the archive, 12-hour incident reporting, surviving confidentiality, audit, countersignature and evidence obligations, no substitution without your written approval, your right to strike the name.
- Publicity clause: equipment-only generic setup, nothing from the collection in frame including screens, glass reflections and wall prints, metadata stripped, exact caption and project page URL, single use, no onward licensing, donor clearance yours.

**Awaiting from you:** the two restricted identifiers to the named operators, sheet verification or a conforming sheet, your incident lead, deputy, mailbox and number, confirmed sheet count, and your review of the specialist undertaking. We will procure and attach their backup attestation once you have approved the undertaking text.

Nothing further open on our side. We will circulate the execution copy on receipt of your contact fields, or earlier with those blank if you prefer to review the rest in parallel.

Please circulate the execution copy now with our incident-contact fields blank so we can review the specialist undertaking in parallel. We will complete those fields before signature. Please attach the signed specialist backup attestation before signature once we approve the undertaking text.

We accept signature before the sheet count is final. The EUR 480 provisioning charge may be invoiced on signature, payable within 30 days. Before capture is scheduled, both parties will sign the one-page amendment recording the confirmed sheet count, billable batch count and total at EUR 220 per batch of up to 250 sheets, exclusive of VAT. Sheet volume alone determines the count. We will send the restricted identifiers privately to the named operators and verify or replace the calibration sheet before scheduling those collections.

For masking, please retain the written clarification process. Hold the affected files while we resolve any ambiguity. A schedule extension applies only if both parties agree in writing that the resolution changes the masking requirements, and only for the actual delay caused.
